title: Fail closed when SRD ancestry extraction under-extracts races
description:
## Problem

The D&D SRD 5.1 importer slices the Races section and then calls parseAncestries. The section anchor failure path is fail-closed, but parseAncestries itself can still return an empty or partial result if the expected race/subrace boundaries are not found inside an otherwise valid slice.

This undermines the deterministic importer goal: a PDF extraction/layout drift could produce a valid-looking rules pack with missing ancestry records.

## Relevant files

- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.ts
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.test.ts or equivalent importer tests

## Requirements

- Add explicit ancestry coverage validation for the SRD 5.1 corpus.
- Fail closed when the parsed ancestry set is empty or missing expected parent/subrace records.
- Include useful diagnostics listing missing expected names.
- Keep section-anchor failures distinct from parser-coverage failures.
- Ensure the failure happens before writing manifest.json / records.json.

## Expected SRD 5.1 coverage

Parent races:
- Dragonborn
- Dwarf
- Elf
- Gnome
- Half-Elf
- Half-Orc
- Halfling
- Human
- Tiefling

Subraces:
- Hill Dwarf
- Mountain Dwarf
- High Elf
- Wood Elf
- Dark Elf (Drow)
- Lightfoot
- Stout
- Forest Gnome
- Rock Gnome

## Acceptance criteria

- A test fixture with a valid races slice but no recognized race headings causes runImporter or the ancestry parsing path to throw.
- A fixture missing one expected ancestry name throws and names the missing record.
- The happy-path SRD import still emits the expected ancestry count.
- Error messages are deterministic and suitable for CI logs.
close_reason: Implemented exact SRD 5.1 ancestry coverage validation before pack writes, with deterministic missing-name diagnostics and no/partial Races fixture coverage; verification passed: npm run typecheck, touched-file Biome CI, npm run test.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Worktree baseline: npm install -> succeeded; npm run typecheck -> passed; npx vitest run packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.test.ts packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/pipeline.test.ts -> passed (47 tests).

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Debugging evidence: parseAncestries returns [] when no known race/subrace headings are found, and runImporter currently passes the resulting ancestries directly to buildPack without a validateAncestryCoverage guard. Working references are validateCreatureCoverage/validateClassCoverage/validateSubclassCoverage/validateFeatureCoverage in index.ts, which run after parsing and before writePackToDirectory. Root cause hypothesis: a valid Races slice can under-extract because ancestry coverage is not validated by expected name set before emit.
